gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch correctly addresses both parts of the issue: (1) deletes the barrel file apps/app/src/components/ui/index.ts and rewires ~84 consumer files (152 import occurrences) to import directly from specific UI modules, and (2) extracts parseLocalFileHref, buildLocalFileAnchorHref, and related types from markdown-preview.tsx into a new markdown-local-file-link.ts module with proper exports. The patch is thorough and consistent.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The verifier would reject the base because the test patch creates a new test file markdown-local-file-link.test.ts that imports from ./markdown-local-file-link.js, which does not exist in the base. The verifier would accept the gold patch because all four test files (including the new one) would resolve their imports and the tested behaviors work correctly. However, the rejection of the base only hinges on the missing new module, not on barrel removal.
too_narrow_risks: No test verifies that the barrel file (apps/app/src/components/ui/index.ts) has been deleted. A candidate could create markdown-local-file-link.ts with correct exports while leaving the barrel intact, and all tests would pass.

Only 2 of 84 files that need import rewiring are covered by the test patch (ProjectRow.test.tsx and ThreadDetailView.test.tsx change their own imports). Since direct imports to specific modules already work on the base (the barrel is additive), these changed test imports pass on both base and gold, providing no signal about the rewiring of the other 82 consumer files.

No TypeScript build check (tsc/turbo typecheck) is run despite the instruction stating 'the TypeScript build should still pass'. A partial solution that creates the new module but doesn't update all consumers (e.g., types.ts still importing from markdown-preview.js) would pass tests but could break the build if markdown-preview.tsx had its exports removed.

A minimal passing solution only needs to create markdown-local-file-link.ts with parseLocalFileHref and buildLocalFileAnchorHref exports matching the expected behavior—no other file changes required to pass all tests.
implementation_coupling: The test file markdown-local-file-link.test.ts imports from the exact path ./markdown-local-file-link.js, coupling to the gold patch's file naming. This is acceptable since the instruction explicitly names this module.

The test patch modifies existing test files to change imports from barrel to direct module paths, which couples the test to the specific import style of the gold patch. However, this is the core behavior being tested.
environment_risks: Tests require pnpm, vitest, and a fully built monorepo (node_modules). The Docker image should provide these, but pnpm workspace builds can be fragile if dependencies aren't fully installed.
The vitest workspace config auto-discovers projects; test resolution depends on the apps/app/vitest.config.ts alias setup mapping @ to ./src being correct.
mismatches: The instruction requires 'the TypeScript build should still pass' but the eval.sh only runs vitest tests, not a typecheck. This means build correctness of the full import rewiring is not verified.

The test patch removes two test cases from markdown-preview.test.tsx (multi-link interception test and deep worktree path test). These behaviors are partially covered by unit tests in the new markdown-local-file-link.test.ts, but the MarkdownPreview integration-level coverage for file:// URL rendering and deep path click handling is lost.

evidence.detail: Only runs 'pnpm exec vitest run' on 4 test files. No tsc/turbo typecheck step despite instruction requiring build to pass.
Creates markdown-local-file-link.test.ts importing from ./markdown-local-file-link.js—this module doesn't exist in base, causing test failure. This is the only mechanism that rejects the base.

ProjectRow.test.tsx and ThreadDetailView.test.tsx only change their own imports from barrel to direct. Direct imports resolve on both base and gold (barrel is additive), so these changes provide no rejection signal.
Barrel file has 250 lines of re-exports used by 84 files (152 import occurrences). No test checks for its deletion.
States 'there should be no remaining consumers of the deleted barrel' but no grep/check for @/components/ui barrel imports is in the test suite.

summary: The gold patch is correct and comprehensive, but the test suite is too narrow: it only verifies the creation of markdown-local-file-link.ts with correct utility exports. The core barrel removal requirement (deleting index.ts and rewiring 84 consumer files with 152 import occurrences) is completely untested. A candidate could pass all tests by creating a single new file without deleting the barrel or changing any imports. Adding a check that index.ts no longer exists and/or that no source files import from @/components/ui would significantly improve coverage. A TypeScript build check would also catch incomplete rewiring.
